To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PT3 project was successful in modeling the NETS-T for all participants and that there was a lack of modeling of the NETS-T Standard 6.

the participants in this study, who were university faculty members and K-12 classroom teachers who were modeling technology integration in their professional practice, did not model Standard 6 of NETS-T, and the levels of cognitive skills needed by students for technology integration activities were not addressed in any of the professional development activities.
the professional development activities we designed and implemented were effective in increasing the knowledge and skills of participants in all areas of the NETS-T except for Standard 6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to help preservice teachers become more competent in technology integration in their classrooms.
how to help teachers become better at integrating technology into their instruction, and we believe that the use of the NETS-T can be a powerful tool to help teachers achieve this goal.
the question: How can technology be integrated into the curriculum in ways that will enhance learning for all students?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

professional development in technology integration is a long-term process and should include a variety of experiences for teachers and faculty to model and practice technology integration in their classrooms and courses.

professional development in technology integration is most successful when it includes modeling of all NETS-T standards and when it includes a focus on ways in which specific pedagogical strategies and software can empower or disempower learners.
professional development activities should include modeling and analysis of all six Standards of the NETS-T. (Contains 3 figures.)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PT3 grant provided the opportunity to model the use of technology to support teaching and learning in a variety of ways.
the PT3 grant has provided an opportunity to work collaboratively and has resulted in increased awareness of the need to integrate technology in all content areas.
technology integration is an ongoing process, which can be enhanced through a combination of professional development and modeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PT3 grant provided a framework for the university faculty members and K-12 educators to work together to improve technology integration in the classroom.
the PT3 grant provided the opportunity to model technology integration for preservice teachers in a way that was not possible before the grant.
technology integration in teacher preparation and K-12 schools is not an easy task, but with a focus on NETS-T and the cognitive skills of learners, the task can be accomplished.
